chapter: Fred Astaire and the high points
title: Director Bud Yorkin checks him out in Detroit
summary: Astaire wanted him vetted, so director Bud Yorkin visited him in Detroit and was satisfied there were no needles lying about.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And he said, "Then they come over to the house. And they said, 'Well, these people, we don't know anything about these people you're talking about. If you want to do a

show get names.'" He says, "Look. This here is what I want to do now, if you want me to do it." So finally after about six weeks they said, "Okay. You can get them and if anything goes wrong it's your fault." So he says okay. So now what they did while I'm playing out at Baker's again, Bud Yorkin is out in the audience and I don't know it. So he was a producer, you know, or a director or something. So he was sitting out there, so I got off after the last set, and he said, "Jonah, my name is Bud Yorkin. I'm the director of the Fred Astaire show. I'd like to go by the hotel and talk to you." So I said I lived in a Soul neighborhood. So we went over there and we started talking, and I was telling him that I was a family man, you know, and I was happy that they selected me for the thing. And he said, "Well, after we selected you, after they decided on you, then Fred Astaire said, "Who knows what type of guy this guy is." So now he began, after he sold them, he said, "You'd better fly in there and check him out." We don't know if he's dopey or what, you know. So after he sat there about two hours that night, he said, "Well, when I go back I think Fred will be very happy. I don't see no needles or nothing laying around. I don't think we'll have no trouble. Because he likes to rehearse." So when I got there they had taken that "St. James Infirmary", off of the record and put it on tape, and the girls are doing all them things to my solo. (Singing). And all that kind of stuff. And I had to learn it over because I don't do it like that every time.
